title: Your first Dockerfile
summary: FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN, ENV, EXPOSE and CMD: what each one does and when it runs.

steps.title: A Dockerfile is a recipe
body: A **Dockerfile** lists the steps that turn source code into an image. `docker build -t myapp .` runs them top to bottom. The `.` is the **build context**: the folder whose files `COPY` can see.
```dockerfile
FROM node:22-alpine                       # start from an image that has Node
WORKDIR /app                              # cd /app (created if missing)
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./    # copy files from the build context
RUN npm ci                                # run a command at BUILD time
COPY . .                                  # copy the rest of the source
ENV NODE_ENV=production                   # environment for later steps and the container
EXPOSE 3000                               # document the port (publishes nothing)
CMD ["node", "server.js"]                 # default command at RUN time
Two moments matter and are easy to mix up:
- **build time** (`docker build`): `FROM`, `WORKDIR`, `COPY`, `RUN` execute and their results are frozen into the image;
- **run time** (`docker run`): only `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT` execute, with the `ENV` values and whatever `-e`, `-p` flags you add.

steps.prompt: Match each instruction to what it does.
pairs: chooses the base image to build on
sets the current directory for the following steps
copies files from the build context into the image
executes a command while building and saves the result
the default command a container runs
documents which port the app listens on

steps.prompt: Does it happen while **building** the image, or when a **container starts**?
steps.explain: A classic bug is putting something that needs run-time information (a database that only exists in production) in a `RUN` step.

steps.prompt: A Dockerfile has `RUN node server.js` as its last line, and no `CMD`. What happens?
options: The build hangs (the server never exits), and even if it finished, containers would not start the server
Containers start the server, because RUN is the start command
Docker rewrites the last RUN into a CMD automatically
The build fails because RUN cannot start Node
steps.explain: `RUN` executes during the build and must finish. The start command belongs in `CMD` (or `ENTRYPOINT`).

steps.prompt: Complete the Dockerfile for a Python app that listens on port 8000.
steps.explain: There is no `CD` instruction: `WORKDIR` both creates the folder and switches to it, and it persists across steps (a `RUN cd /app` would not).

steps.title: Shell form and exec form
body: `RUN`, `CMD` and `ENTRYPOINT` accept two forms:
```dockerfile
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl     # shell form: run by /bin/sh -c "..."
CMD ["dotnet", "Api.dll"]                         # exec form: a JSON array, no shell
- **Shell form** gives you `&&`, pipes and `$VARIABLES`. Good for `RUN`.
- **Exec form** runs the program directly. Use it for `CMD` and `ENTRYPOINT`, so your app is PID 1 and receives the stop signal (more on that in the next lesson).
Exec form must be valid JSON: **double** quotes. `CMD ['node', 'server.js']` is silently treated as shell form and breaks.
Instructions are case-insensitive, but everyone writes them in UPPER CASE. A `\` at the end of a line continues the instruction on the next line.

steps.prompt: Arrange this Dockerfile for a Python web app. Copy the requirements file and install it **before** copying the rest of the code, so installs are cached.
steps.explain: `FROM` is always first. `WORKDIR` before the copies, because `.` means the working directory. You will see exactly why the install comes before `COPY . .` in the caching lesson.

steps.prompt: Which `CMD` line is written correctly in exec form?
steps.explain: Exec form is a JSON array of strings, and JSON requires double quotes.

steps.title: List the instructions
prompt: Write `List<string> Instructions(List<string> lines)` that reads a Dockerfile and returns one entry per instruction: `"N KEYWORD arguments"`, numbered from 1.
- Skip blank lines and comment lines (starting with `#` after trimming).
- The keyword is upper-cased (`run` → `RUN`); arguments are trimmed.
- A line ending in `\` continues on the next line: drop the `\`, trim each piece and join the pieces with one space.
workdir /app                         3 RUN apk add --no-cache curl && npm ci
template: Dojo.Eq("simple file", new List<string> { "1 FROM node:22-alpine", "2 WORKDIR /app", "3 COPY . .", "4 CMD [\"node\", \"server.js\"]" }, Instructions(new List<string> { "FROM node:22-alpine", "WORKDIR /app", "COPY . .", "CMD [\"node\", \"server.js\"]" }));

Dojo.Eq("comments, blanks and lower case", new List<string> { "1 FROM alpine:3.20", "2 RUN echo hi" }, Instructions(new List<string> { "# a comment", "", "from alpine:3.20", "   ", "  run   echo hi  " }));

Dojo.Eq("line continuations", new List<string> { "1 FROM node:22-alpine", "2 RUN apk add --no-cache curl && npm ci", "3 EXPOSE 3000" }, Instructions(new List<string> { "FROM node:22-alpine", "RUN apk add --no-cache curl \\", "    && npm ci", "EXPOSE 3000" }));
Dojo.Eq("three-line continuation", new List<string> { "1 RUN a && b && c" }, Instructions(new List<string> { "RUN a \\", "  && b \\", "  && c" }));
hints: Keep a `pending` string for an instruction that is still being continued.
Only skip blank and comment lines when nothing is pending.
Split the finished instruction at its first space into keyword and arguments.
